summary: The existing recipe (restore_um21_tread_components.py) cannot run the post-decision scope: it requires all 50 baseline records and 8,626 observations. With D-UM21-T02-1 = A the scope is 44 records and 7,562 observations. The T02 runner handles one record. New runner contributor_tools/run_um21_t03_full.py leaves every bound file unchanged, narrows the producer input to a batch of records, runs the unchanged producer once per batch and the unchanged audit once per record. Four batches of 11 records, four guarded jobs, run one at a time. Nothing launched, no dry run, no research data read beyond hashing bindings.

memory_analysis.producer: extend_umich_tread_source.py streams: one 150-row batch (one observation) at a time through pyarrow iter_batches and a ParquetWriter; the only per-record state kept is a small summary dict entry. The readback also streams 150-row batches. No full-record or full-dataset arrays are held, so peak memory does not scale with record count. Remaining doubt: a long-lived process keeps the h5py handle (1 MiB chunk cache per dataset) and allocator fragmentation across records; pilot peaks were 88 MiB (census, one record), about 160 MiB (v4 sign pilot, 7 records) and 214 MiB (T02 pilot, one record, producer plus audit steps).
memory_analysis.audit: audit_um21_tread_pilot.py takes one subject/condition per process and self-guards at 300 MiB; it is a fresh process per record, so its 182 MiB peak does not accumulate.
memory_analysis.decision: Projected peak is about 220 MiB per job, below the 600 MiB threshold, but because of the producer's long-lived process the run is split anyway: 4 batches of 11 records (11 of 44 bounds the producer lifetime at a quarter of the work). Per-record outputs depend only on the record, so batches give the same files as one full run; each batch has its own receipt. No limit raised; every job runs under the guarded launcher (3.5 GiB free to start, 768 MiB address space, kill under 2 GiB).
memory_analysis.timing_estimate: Not measured. T02 pilot: 71.9 s with two source hashes. A batch hashes the 2.2 GB source once in the producer plus once per audit (11); expected roughly 10-15 minutes per batch against the 3,600 s launcher cap. Step timeouts: producer 1,800 s, each audit 400 s.

runner_design.scope: python3 contributor_tools/run_um21_t03_full.py scope --out FILE: reads baseline summary, baseline readback and clock census (small JSON); refuses unless the readback matches the summary and source, every census name is in the baseline, kept plus dropped equals the baseline, and the kept count and observations equal the census totals.
runner_design.run: stages the batch's baseline phase.parquet and candidate_ledger.jsonl bit-identical (hash-checked against summary and readback) into a new base root in baseline order, writes a narrowed summary and readback, runs the unchanged producer once, requires its summary to be complete with the exact batch membership and observation counts equal to the scope, then runs the unchanged audit per record into audit/<subject>_<condition>/ with the expected source sha256. All audits run even if one fails. Exit 0 only if every audit passes.
runner_design.imports: imports run_um21_t02_pilot.py (digest, run_step, peak_rss_mib, paths); both are bound by hash in the specs.

batch2.status: failed, exit 1, clean_success false; verify-cleanup proven
batch2.cause: Producer (extend_umich_tread_source.py, unchanged) died with OSError errno 12 Cannot allocate memory while reading Streaming.mat (HDF5) and then closing the Parquet writer, after converting 5 records (AB06 d10, d5, i0, i10, i5; 197+184+169+169+157 = 876 observations) and during the 6th (AB06 i5 finished; AB07 folder started). RSS stayed about 216 MiB, so this is the 768 MiB address-space cap (virtual size), not physical memory or the free-memory guard. Address space grows over a long-lived producer process (h5py/arrow mappings), so my RSS-based claim that memory does not grow with records was wrong for virtual size. Batches 0 and 1 (11 records each) fit; batch 2 did not. No audits ran for batch 2. Partial outputs remain under the batch 2 output root and are not valid output.
batch2.proposed_fix_for_review: Smaller batches (e.g. 5 records per job, 5 more jobs for the remaining 22 records including re-doing batch 2) with a new scope/batch partition and new specs and output roots; the existing batch 2 root must not be reused or deleted without review. Requires reviewing a change to the scope file batching only; no bound file changes. Not decided.

virtual_size_investigation.finding: AB07 is not heavier. Metadata-only probe (shapes and chunking, no arrays, 43 MiB RSS): every AB05-AB08 Tread record has the same 28 joint datasets, about 11 MiB of joint data (AB08 i10 13 MiB, being dropped), 17,000-18,000 frames, chunks of 2,430-2,570 frames. The failing read at file offset about 1.377 GB was a 41 KB read, so the process ran out of address space, not a large read. Batches 0 and 1 converted 11 records each within the same cap while batch 2 died during the 6th, so virtual growth per record is not fixed (allocator/mapping behaviour of the long-lived producer); the cause is not determined and I have no measurement of the producer virtual size.
virtual_size_investigation.implication: One record per batch for AB07 is not indicated by record size. The 5-record batches rest on batch 2 having finished 5 records; if a v2 batch fails again, go to one-two records per job. Not measured.
